Semicolon Alt Code and Symbol

The Alt code for Semicolon is 59. Hold Alt, type 59 on the numeric keypad, then release Alt. Semicolon also has the Unicode codepoint U+003B, so you can type it with Alt+59 on Windows, search for U+003B in macOS's Character Viewer, use ; in HTML, or \003B in CSS. If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, use the Character Viewer, the HTML entity, or copy the character directly — the Alt key method requires a physical numpad. Copy the Semicolon character from this page when you need it in a form, chat message or document that does not accept Alt codes. Semicolon has no named HTML entity, so use the numeric escape ; or the hex escape ;.

How to type semicolon on Windows

  1. Turn Num Lock on so the numeric keypad is active.
  2. Hold the left Alt key.
  3. Type 5 9 on the numeric keypad.
  4. Release Alt. The Semicolon character (;) appears.

If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, see how to type symbols without a numpad.

How to type semicolon on macOS

There is no direct Option shortcut for Semicolon. Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space, search for "Semicolon" and click the character to insert it.

How to use semicolon in code

  • HTML: or
  • CSS: content:"\003B"; ()
  • Python: \u003B or chr(0x3B)
  • JavaScript: \u003B or String.fromCodePoint(0x3B)
  • JSON: "\u003B"

Frequently asked questions

What is the Alt code for Semicolon?

The legacy Alt code for Semicolon is 59. Hold Alt, type 5 9 on the numeric keypad, then release Alt.

How do I type ; without a numpad?

Use the Windows Character Viewer (Win+.), the macOS Character Viewer (⌃⌘Space), an HTML entity such as ;, or copy the character directly from this page.

Why does Alt+59 not work?

Alt+59 only works on a keyboard with a physical numeric keypad. It also requires the application to accept the numeric-keypad input path. Laptops without a numpad need an alternative method.

What is the Unicode for Semicolon?

The Unicode codepoint for Semicolon is U+003B. You can use this value in HTML as ;, in CSS as \003B, and in Word with Alt+X.

How do I type ; on a Mac?

Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space and search for the character name or U+003B, then click it.
